summary: Slovakia is an EU and Schengen member: EU/EEA citizens need no visa, nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation 2018/1806), including the US, the UK and Japan, can stay 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-required list (Annex I) need a Schengen visa.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

The UK government says that if you need the Slovak Mountain Rescue Service (HZS) you will have to meet costs of up to €1,000, advises making sure your insurance includes rescue costs, and says ignoring HZS rules or instructions can bring a fine of up to €3,320.
Visa-waiver nationals will need an ETIAS travel authorization once the EU system starts; the EU says it is not yet in operation.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Slovakia?
faq.answer: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens need no visa. Nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation 2018/1806), including the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and Japan, can stay 90 days in any 180-day period. Nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-required list (Annex I) need a Schengen visa.

faq.question: Is Slovakia in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says Slovakia follows Schengen area rules, and tells British travellers that visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before they travel count towards their 90 days.

faq.question: Will I need ETIAS for Slovakia?
faq.answer: Once the EU's ETIAS system starts, visa-waiver travelers will need the online authorization before their trip. The EU says it will cost €20 (free for under-18s and over-70s), be valid for three years or until the passport expires, and that it is not yet in operation.

faq.question: What currency does Slovakia use?
faq.answer: The euro, according to Canada's travel advice.
